brief: Custom-fit leather handbags, Italian-made, handcrafted in Florence. Minimum order ships in 6 weeks. Average price point $1,200.

profile.business_summary: A luxury DTC brand offering custom-fit leather handbags that are Italian-made and handcrafted in Florence.

relevant_tags.why: Handbags are a core fashion accessory adjacent to apparel.
High-end luxury handcrafted items can serve as significant gifts.
Handcrafted goods often align with slow fashion and durability.

note_signals.why: Older affluent women with high AOV who respond to quality messaging align well with luxury handbags.
Highest-AOV apparel publisher with a conservative brand sensibility matches luxury Italian craftsmanship.

profile.gate_reason: Product, pricing, and origin are clearly stated, allowing for precise network placement among high-AOV fashion publishers.

config.advertiser_summary: A luxury DTC brand offering custom-fit leather handbags that are Italian-made and handcrafted in Florence.

assumptions: No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 60% gross margin (typical for apparel). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($1200 x 60% margin x 1.1 orders = $792.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $554.40 x click-to-purchase rate (1.0%-3.5% for apparel). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.15 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $6.00 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.14 -> relative fit x1.36 on CTR/CVR; max bid $6.00 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $6,350, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.
Budget too small for Stride & Stem: concentrating on fewer hosts.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $554.40 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
